Series::view¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::view(pluss::msharp::RangeView::Int new_sizes) const -> Series

What It Does¶

Reinterprets the same underlying storage with a different shape, without copying, when the current layout is view-compatible.

In the current implementation that requirement is strict: view() only accepts layouts that are already contiguous and shape-compatible. If the source is non-contiguous, view() throws instead of silently materializing a copy.

That makes view() the “I want a true layout reinterpretation” API. If you want “same logical result, copy if needed”, use reshape() instead.

Parameters¶

new_sizes (pluss::msharp::RangeView::Int)

The desired output shape.

view() requires:

  • the same total element count as the source

  • a shape that the source can be viewed as directly

  • a contiguous source layout in the current implementation

If that contract is not met, the call throws. The most visible current failure message is "view: requires contiguous in v0".

Returns¶

Series A new Series handle over the same storage, with new_sizes and freshly computed contiguous strides for that shape.

Examples¶

Example 1. Reinterpret a contiguous 2 x 3 series as 3 x 2.

auto mat = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, {2, 3});
const std::array<std::int64_t, 2> shape_3x2{{3, 2}};

std::cout << mat.view(
    std::span<const std::int64_t>(shape_3x2.data(), shape_3x2.size()));

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 2],
  [3, 4],
  [5, 6]]

Nothing was transposed here; the same flat storage is simply re-read under a new shape. That is why the rows become [1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6].

Example 2. A transposed series is non-contiguous, so view() rejects it rather than copying.

try {
  auto transposed = mat.transpose(0, 1);
  std::cout << transposed.view(
      std::span<const std::int64_t>(shape_3x2.data(), shape_3x2.size()));
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

view: requires contiguous in v0

This is the key boundary between view() and reshape(): once the layout stops being directly viewable, view() stays strict.

Notes¶

  • view() is the no-copy path; it is supposed to fail rather than quietly allocate.

  • The output shape must preserve total numel().

  • If you already know the source may be non-contiguous, reach for reshape() directly.

See Also¶

  • Series::reshape: same high-level shape change, but with a contiguous fallback when a true view is impossible.

  • Series::slice: another view-producing layout change, but by range restriction instead of shape reinterpretation.
